skipped_revisions.author: safety_engineer
skipped_revisions.description: Separated this functional safety requirement (ISO 26262 Part 4) from FB2-HW-TSR-000004 (Part 5), which carried identical statement, rationale, safety_allocation and acceptance_criteria, and made the shared 'All cells (or representative subset >= 50%)' coverage criterion measurable. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000027. This record now states the safety intent and only acceptance criteria that a test can decide from the item's observable behaviour: that the reaction is retained while the main microcontroller is held in reset (100 percent of overvoltage test points), the independent detection latency of 50 ms, and the 50 mV threshold accuracy. The structural properties - which rails, references, driver stages and comparators are shared with the main chain, and how many cells the independent chain covers - are hardware design properties and now live only in FB2-HW-TSR-000004, which states the hardware obligation with its own hardware acceptance criteria. The coverage criterion is resolved to 100 percent of the cells the main measurement chain monitors: the 'representative subset >= 50%' branch was rejected because 'representative subset' is undefined, no selection method is recorded anywhere in the corpus, and a subset would leave cells with no barrier against a main-path failure, which is the barrier's purpose. The 100 percent figure follows the precedent already used by FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 ('All cell voltages acquired / Cell count match / 100 / %'). The feasibility of a full independent divider network is NOT asserted: FB2-ASM-008 already records it as 'Requires PCB space, separate power domain, additional BOM cost. Feasibility to be confirmed', and that assumption is unchanged by this revision. The ASIL (ASIL_B), the safety_goal_ref, the statement's 50 ms and the verification approach are unchanged. The 115 ms figure in the rationale was removed in the same revision under finding FB2-REV-FND-000026. Removed the 115 ms figure from the rationale and replaced it with arithmetic derived from the corpus's own parameter registry. Finding FB2-REV-FND-000026 reported 115 ms as appearing in no record; that part of its evidence is corrected here. The figure is real but stale: it is the sum of a superseded allocation recorded in FB2-REV-000001 (as_is vertical-slice review, embedded finding FB2-FND-000001) as 'FSR-001 specifies 10 Hz (100 ms); FSR-002 specifies 10 ms check; FSR-003 specifies 5 ms contactor; sum = 115 ms'. 100 + 10 + 5 = 115. The allocation has since changed - FB2-PRM-000003 now gives afe_acquisition_period_ms = 50 and FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 allocates 25 ms for acquisition - so the figure no longer describes anything in this corpus. The justification is now stated on figures that still hold: the main path is 85 ms of the 100 ms interval; at the 40 ms upper tolerance of FB2-PRM-000005 the contactor chain is 5 + 40 + 5 = 50 ms and the main path is 95 ms; and if detection waits one full acquisition period of FB2-PRM-000003 (50 ms) rather than the 25 ms allocated, the main path is 85 - 25 + 50 = 110 ms and overruns the interval. A main-path-only reaction therefore has no tolerance for a degraded contactor or for one acquisition period, which is the substantive argument for a second barrier and does not need the 115 ms. FB2-ASM-008's rationale carried the same stale figure and was corrected in the same pass.

skipped_revisions.author: safety_engineer
skipped_revisions.description: Added the fault_reaction this requirement was missing. AR-005 is one of the four elements the FSC allocates a reaction to, and the reaction is the second barrier itself: open the contactors from the independent path, without waiting for the main microcontroller, at 50 ms, which is FB2-PRM-000007. The field records that this budget is an ALTERNATIVE to the main path's and not an addition to it - the two sum to 135 ms against a 100 ms interval, which is why the FSC and TSC both justify the barrier as a sensitivity on the main path (85 ms nominal, 95 ms at the FB2-PRM-000005 upper tolerance, 110 ms if detection waits a full acquisition period) rather than as a sum. mode_dependence states the property the concepts both insist on: there is no mode arbitration in this path, so in MOD-004 a hardware false positive disconnects a moving vehicle with no software able to intervene, and that is why the 50 mV threshold accuracy is a safety requirement in its own right. open_limits states the limit that dominates this record: the independence the reaction depends on is FB2-ASM-008, an assumption, is not demonstrated anywhere in this corpus, and the TSC names the absence of that demonstration as the largest open assumption of the ASIL D allocation. Revision 2 -> 3. Statement, rationale, all three acceptance criteria, safety_allocation including the ASIL_B allocation, feasibility_dependencies and the safety goal reference are unchanged and no threshold was relaxed. Human approval remains pending, production_authorized stays false and product_verification_credit stays false.

skipped_revisions.author: safety_engineer
skipped_revisions.description: Corrected timing_budget.allocation.margin_ms from 20 to 15 so that the recorded budget closes. The ten serial elements of the allocation sum to 85 ms (25+5+2+3+5+2+3+5+30+5) and the fault tolerant time interval is 100 ms, so the margin available is 100-85 = 15 ms; the recorded 20 ms exceeded the time that was available and made the budget total 105 ms against a 100 ms interval. A margin is a derived quantity - the difference between the interval and the work - not a measured one, so 15 ms is the only value the interval admits. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000025. The two alternative repairs were considered and rejected on the corpus's own evidence: raising the FTTI to 105 ms would contradict FB2-PRM-000004, which fixes ftti_ms = 100 with tolerance min = max = 100 and calibration by safety analysis against the HARA, and would define the interval from the answer; shrinking the serial sum to 80 ms would delete work that traces to a parameter or an assumption. The 85 ms serial figure is unchanged and is the figure FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 already recomputed independently. 15 ms is also the margin the technical safety concept already published, so this change removes the departure between the two records rather than creating one. The 105 ms total was NOT rounded down to 100 ms: the arithmetic now closes because 85 + 15 = 100, not because a number was adjusted to look equal. The FTTI value, all ten serial allocations, the statement, the safe state, the degraded state and the ASIL are unchanged.

skipped_revisions.author: safety_engineer
skipped_revisions.description: Added the asil_justification the ASIL assignment validator required and did not find. The field is a derivation, not a restatement: severity, exposure, controllability and the operational situation are copied from the HE-01 entry of FB2-SAF-HAZ-000001 in this same profile, the ASIL is then RECOMPUTED from the ISO 26262-3:2018 severity/exposure determination table and compared with what this record and the hazard record already claimed. They agree - S3 with E4 gives ASIL_D, and the second hazardous event HE-02 at S2/E3 gives ASIL_B, which is also what that entry already claimed - so there was no contradiction between the S/E/C values and the ASIL to resolve, and neither was changed. What the derivation adds is the working: the reasoning behind each rating, the whole S3 row so the sensitivity of the answer is visible, the inheritance of the higher ASIL from the two events the goal covers, and the consistency check against the allocation beneath it, where an ASIL B second barrier is admissible precisely because it is not the sole means of achieving an ASIL D goal. The field also states what it does not assert, at length and specifically: this is a hypothetical classification inside a fictional reference project, the real foxBMS 2 product has never had a hazard analysis and risk assessment and no ASIL is determined for it, the S/E/C ratings are authored inputs that were not obtained from any exposure analysis, mission profile, fleet statistic, FMEA or measurement, no design is claimed to meet ASIL D, no conformity with ISO 26262 and no certification is claimed, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no ASPICE capability level is claimed. The exposure rating is flagged as the unevidenced input on which the whole classification turns, because S3 with E3 would be ASIL_C - one class lower - and nothing in this corpus establishes the exposure. Nothing else in the record changed: the asil value, the statement, the safe state, the degraded state, the fault_tolerant_time_interval_ms and the whole timing_budget allocation including the 15 ms margin that FB2-REV-FND-000025 reconciled are untouched. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. Remediation of the ASIL-assignment finding on this record. This is the synthetic_reference copy, the one both safety concepts derive from. Its hazard record states the operational situation to the granularity a C3 assessment requires - 'CHARGING mode, high SOC (>90%), fast charge (>1C), ambient > 45 degC' rather than 'while charging' - and the field records that specificity as the corpus's own evidence that a controllability assessment was applied rather than asserted. It also states the scope limit explicitly: FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 both carry concept_identity.fictional = true, so the classification describes a fictional reference project and establishes no property of any real product.

skipped_revisions.author: safety_engineer
skipped_revisions.description: Bound the fault tolerant time interval to the parameter that fixes it, so the interval has one authoritative home instead of three. Added the ftti.parameter_ref field naming FB2-PRM-000004. The record previously restated the interval twice on itself - fault_tolerant_time_interval_ms and timing_budget.total_ftti_ms - while the authoritative value lived in the parameter registry as ftti_ms = 100 with tolerance min = max = 100, and neither the record nor the registry pointed at the other. The ftti budget consistency checker read a third spelling, ftti_ms or ftti, which no safety goal in this corpus carried, so it could never fire on this record and SCN-MUT-006 had no detector. The rule now resolves the interval from the bound parameter and requires every declaration on the record to agree with it, so the three spellings are now cross-checked instead of merely coexisting; a drift in any of them is reported. Neither of the two existing declarations was removed: the technical safety concept and several review records read them, and deleting them would move a value rather than bind it. The interval value is unchanged at 100 ms, the ASIL is unchanged at ASIL_D, the ten serial allocations and the 15 ms margin are unchanged, and the budget still closes at 85 + 15 = 100 ms. skipped_revisions.description: Reconciled the contactor reaction figures, which gave three different numbers for one chain: a 30 ms acceptance threshold, 35 ms in this record's own rationale and 40 ms in the safety goal's timing budget. skipped_revisions.author: cybersecurity_engineer
skipped_revisions.description: Replaced the absolute '0 genuine frames rejected over 24 h' acceptance criterion with a bounded rate, a stated population the bound is demonstrated over, and a minimum integrity value width that makes the bound achievable. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000028. The old criterion was unsatisfiable and non-discriminating at the same time: a keyed integrity value of width w rejects a genuine frame with probability 2^-w, so over a 24 h campaign the expected number of genuine rejections is n * 2^-w, non-zero for any practical w; meanwhile an implementation that rejected every frame would satisfy the criterion vacuously, and would also satisfy the other criteria in this record vacuously. The new criterion is 0 rejections observed over a genuine-frame population of at least 3 x 10^6 in a 24 h campaign, which by the rule of three (0 failures in n trials gives a one-sided 95 percent upper bound of 3/n) is a bound of 1 x 10^-6 on the rate; and it requires the integrity value on the interface to be at least 22 bits, which is the width for which 2^-w stays below that rate over that population. The three statements are mutually consistent, so the criterion is now achievable by a correct implementation of adequate width and is not satisfied by an always-rejecting one (~100 percent) or by a 16-bit one (~1.5e-5 per frame). The criterion is therefore STRICTER in discriminating power than the zero it replaces, and it is also a harder engineering obligation, because it constrains the width of the integrity value where the zero constrained nothing. The absolute zeros that remain in this record are the ones that are decidable by the check existing - injected frames accepted, replayed frames accepted, length-mismatch frames reaching the callback, control-byte transitions - and those are over countable events on a channel where no collision is involved, so they are unchanged and were deliberately not relaxed. The verification measure FB2-VER-TMS-000018 and its execution record were regenerated against the new criterion in the same revision set. No ASIL value, safety_goal_ref, statement clause or verification approach was changed.

skipped_revisions.author: cybersecurity_engineer
skipped_revisions.description: Replaced the absolute '0 genuine frames rejected over 24 h' acceptance criterion with a bounded rate, a stated population the bound is demonstrated over, and a minimum integrity value width that makes the bound achievable. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000028. The old criterion was unsatisfiable and non-discriminating at the same time: a keyed integrity value of width w rejects a genuine frame with probability 2^-w, so over a 24 h campaign the expected number of genuine rejections is n * 2^-w, non-zero for any practical w; meanwhile an implementation that rejected every frame would satisfy the criterion vacuously, and would also satisfy the other criteria in this record vacuously. The new criterion is 0 rejections observed over a genuine-frame population of at least 3 x 10^6 in a 24 h campaign, which by the rule of three (0 failures in n trials gives a one-sided 95 percent upper bound of 3/n) is a bound of 1 x 10^-6 on the rate; and it requires the integrity value on the interface to be at least 22 bits, which is the width for which 2^-w stays below that rate over that population. The three statements are mutually consistent, so the criterion is now achievable by a correct implementation of adequate width and is not satisfied by an always-rejecting one (~100 percent) or by a 16-bit one (~1.5e-5 per frame). The criterion is therefore STRICTER in discriminating power than the zero it replaces, and it is also a harder engineering obligation, because it constrains the width of the integrity value where the zero constrained nothing. The absolute zeros that remain in this record are the ones that are decidable by the check existing - injected frames accepted, replayed frames accepted, length-mismatch frames reaching the callback, control-byte transitions - and those are over countable events on a channel where no collision is involved, so they are unchanged and were deliberately not relaxed. The verification measure FB2-VER-TMS-000018 and its execution record were regenerated against the new criterion in the same revision set. No ASIL value, safety_goal_ref, statement clause or verification approach was changed.

skipped_revisions.author: safety_engineer
skipped_revisions.description: Separated this functional safety requirement (ISO 26262 Part 4) from FB2-HW-TSR-000004 (Part 5), which carried identical statement, rationale, safety_allocation and acceptance_criteria, and made the shared 'All cells (or representative subset >= 50%)' coverage criterion measurable. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000027. This record now states the safety intent and only acceptance criteria that a test can decide from the item's observable behaviour: that the reaction is retained while the main microcontroller is held in reset (100 percent of overvoltage test points), the independent detection latency of 50 ms, and the 50 mV threshold accuracy. The structural properties - which rails, references, driver stages and comparators are shared with the main chain, and how many cells the independent chain covers - are hardware design properties and now live only in FB2-HW-TSR-000004, which states the hardware obligation with its own hardware acceptance criteria. The coverage criterion is resolved to 100 percent of the cells the main measurement chain monitors: the 'representative subset >= 50%' branch was rejected because 'representative subset' is undefined, no selection method is recorded anywhere in the corpus, and a subset would leave cells with no barrier against a main-path failure, which is the barrier's purpose. The 100 percent figure follows the precedent already used by FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 ('All cell voltages acquired / Cell count match / 100 / %'). The feasibility of a full independent divider network is NOT asserted: FB2-ASM-008 already records it as 'Requires PCB space, separate power domain, additional BOM cost. Feasibility to be confirmed', and that assumption is unchanged by this revision. The ASIL (ASIL_B), the safety_goal_ref, the statement's 50 ms and the verification approach are unchanged. The 115 ms figure in the rationale was removed in the same revision under finding FB2-REV-FND-000026. Removed the 115 ms figure from the rationale and replaced it with arithmetic derived from the corpus's own parameter registry. Finding FB2-REV-FND-000026 reported 115 ms as appearing in no record; that part of its evidence is corrected here. links.rationale: FB2-SW-IMP-000001 realises the reference project's FB2-SW-SWR-000001 at the requirement level: acquisition is triggered through AFE_StartMeasurement into the LTC sequencer, integrity is gated by LTC_CheckPec before parsed values reach the database block, and publication is the DATA_WRITE_DATA path whose database handler stamps a header timestamp. The requirement's 20 Hz, 5 ms and 100% figures are not established by this link.

FB2-SW-IMP-000002 realises the comparison clause of the reference project's FB2-SW-SWR-000002 and, at revision 1, does not realise its debounce clause: the implementation record declares the missing per-cell debounce counter as a not_in_source proposal, so this link asserts partial realisation and says which part is missing.

FB2-SW-IMP-000003 realises the actuation and feedback-confirmation clauses of the reference project's FB2-SW-SWR-000003, with the sequencing realised one layer above in BMS_Trigger, and declares the design's cycle counter a not_in_source proposal. The requirement's 5 ms emergency-open clause is not established by this link and the configured waits the source applies are longer.

FB2-SW-IMP-000004 is the implementation element the reference project relies on for FB2-SYS-SYR-000007: the periodic BMS-state frame is the publication mechanism for the item's own mode. The link asserts partial realisation only - the requirement's limit-publication and diagnosable-refusal criteria have no code path in the pinned source and the refusal is declared as a not_in_source proposal on the implementation record.

skipped_revisions.description: Added the asil_justification that the requirement applicability validator requires and did not find: this record marks safety_allocation.asil as not_applicable, which requirement.schema.json enumerates as the value for a requirement to which no ASIL determination applies, and the rule requires a recorded reason for that marking. The reason had been present only inside safety_allocation.mitigation and safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref, which are required on every requirement whatever its marking and are therefore populated identically on the ASIL_D records; they cannot serve as a justification specific to this marking. The new field states the reason on its own, names what the safety_goal_ref trace does and does not carry, and records the open items where the marking depends on something not yet established. The asil value, the statement, the mitigation, the safety_goal_ref and the revision-relevant content of the record are unchanged. Remediation of the requirement applicability validator finding raised by finding FB2-REV-FND-000032. Nothing in this field asserts ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level or human approval; human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.

links.rationale: FB2-SW-SWR-000001 is allocated to the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000001 as the software requirement whose implementation that design details. Direction is requirement -> design element, as master prompt section 13 declares for allocated_to.
FB2-SW-SWR-000002 is allocated to the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000002 as the software requirement whose implementation that design details. Direction is requirement -> design element.

FB2-SW-SWR-000003 is allocated to the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000003 as the software requirement whose implementation that design details. The design additionally claims sequencing and cycle counting the requirement does not state and the source does not realise; that difference is recorded on the implementation record rather than hidden by this link.

This measure is the source-grounded part of FB2-SYS-SYR-000001's verification: it decides the requirement's integrity-before-use and data-age criteria against the mechanism the pinned source defines, namely the per-LTC packet error code comparison and the database header timestamp. The link asserts those two criteria only; the requirement's acquisition-rate criterion is deliberately not covered here and is covered by FB2-VER-TMS-000022 under a different oracle kind.

This measure is the analytical part of FB2-SYS-SYR-000001's verification: it computes whether the configured acquisition period meets the requirement's rate threshold, and records the margin, which at the registry's 50 ms period is zero. It exists as a separate measure from FB2-VER-TMS-000021 so that a source-grounded pass on integrity cannot be mistaken for a pass on rate.

This measure is the source-grounded part of FB2-SYS-SYR-000002's verification: it establishes, from the nested tier comparison and the diagnosis configuration table at the pinned commit, that an excursion into the two outer tiers is graded below the safety-limit tier and cannot reach the fault reaction. It covers the requirement's degradation-discrimination criterion and not its debounce or its declared boundary.

This measure is the assumption-based part of FB2-SYS-SYR-000002's verification: it addresses the debounce and the degraded-to-fault boundary, neither of which has any counterpart in the pinned source, and it declares the assumption its outcomes rest on rather than presenting them as verified behaviour. Its paired execution record is blocked, so this link asserts that a planned verification exists and not that the requirement is met.

This measure is the analytical verification of FB2-SYS-SYR-000003: it sums the waits the pinned source's application configuration applies between the stages of opening and compares the total against the interval the requirement allocates, and it expects the comparison to fail. The link asserts that the timing claim is under verification and under contradicted, not that the requirement is satisfied.

This measure is the source-grounded verification of FB2-SYS-SYR-000004's mode-dependent reaction criterion: it establishes from the pinned source that the applicable temperature tier set is selected by the sign of the string current and that the admissibility of an initialisation request is selected by the current state. The link asserts coverage of that criterion only; the requirement's mode-publication criterion is not covered.

This measure is the only verification FB2-SYS-SYR-000005 has, and it verifies the requirement against the corpus's own declared assumption because the second-barrier element it describes does not exist in either profile. The link is deliberately weak and says so: it records that a planned verification exists against an assumption, and its paired execution record is blocked because there is nothing to execute against.

This measure is the source-grounded verification of FB2-SYS-SYR-000006's validity-marking and envelope-check criteria, established from the pinned source's current-sensor receive callback and the SOA module's gating on the invalid flag. The link asserts coverage of two of the requirement's three criteria; the third, that no invalid measurement reaches any supervisory decision, needs a consumer census this measure does not contain.
